input.prompt: A colored-pencil drawing on cream paper comes to life, hand-drawn in every frame: same pencil lines, paper and hatching as the first frame, never a photo or 3D. Lip sync first: she sings '(held note) because my imagination is linked to my everyday' from the reference audio, each syllable on the voice, lips shut on b and m: after a held note, lips press together on the 'b' of 'because', then the mouth stays open, never closing, through the long held 'cause'; lips pressing together on the 'm' of 'my' and the 'm' of 'imagination', opening wide on 'a'. She acts the lyric like a music-video performer, thinking it through as she sings: her shoulders, arms and hands move with clear, motivated gestures; her face shows each thought. The idea arrives. Through the held note and 'because' her eyes drift up and off to the side, as if she can see past the edge of the page, lips parted in wonder; on 'imagination' she lifts one hand and taps her temple with a fingertip, eyes lighting up; on 'is linked' both hands open outward from her head, palms up, like the world unfolding along the drawn chain of everyday things beside her; on 'everyday' she turns back to the camera with a big grin and a nod. Same person as in the first frame: large head, heart-shaped face, soft chin, tall forehead with the high centre-parted hairline, the two slightly different eyebrows, the same big dark-brown eyes; do not restyle her face. Her hair stays up in the bun with the two yellow pencils crossing through it in an X, both eraser caps pointing up (one blue, one pink); the pencils move only with her head and never fall; her hands stay empty. Headphones stay round her neck; the white jacket keeps its horizontal orange bands, ONE small pale-blue chest dot where it is and ONE round 1420 MHz patch on the orange band of her upper arm. The camera drifts slowly and gently in toward her, keeping her face, shoulders and hands in frame. One continuous shot, no cuts. No captions, no text, no new objects.
